scenes.heading: Delta Lake MERGE & Upserts
scenes.narration: Let's take a deep look at Delta Lake MERGE & Upserts and how it works under the hood in Spark.

scenes.heading: What MERGE gives you
items: Atomic upserts: update, insert, delete in one op
ACID transactions on a data lake
Ideal for CDC and slowly changing dims
scenes.narration: Delta Lake's MERGE brings database-style upserts to the data lake, letting you update, insert, and delete rows in a single atomic operation. Because Delta provides ACID transactions, the whole MERGE either fully succeeds or leaves the table untouched. This makes it the natural tool for applying change-data-capture streams and maintaining slowly changing dimension tables.

scenes.heading: How a MERGE executes
steps: Join source to target on keys
scenes.narration: A MERGE first joins the incoming source against the target table on the match keys. Rows that match existing keys are updated or deleted according to your clauses, while rows with no match are inserted as new records. All of these changes are written and then committed atomically through Delta's transaction log. Readers only ever see the state before or after the commit, never a partial result.

scenes.code:
from delta.tables import DeltaTable

target = DeltaTable.forPath(spark, "/delta/customers")
(target.alias("t")
  .merge(updates.alias("s"), "t.id = s.id")
  .whenMatchedUpdate(set={"name": "s.name", "email": "s.email"})
  .whenNotMatchedInsert(values={"id": "s.id", "name": "s.name", "email": "s.email"})
  .execute())
scenes.heading: A classic upsert
scenes.narration: Here we open the customers Delta table and merge a batch of updates on the id key. The whenMatchedUpdate clause refreshes the name and email of existing customers, while whenNotMatchedInsert adds brand-new customers that were not already present. Calling execute runs the whole operation as one atomic transaction. This single statement replaces the fragile read-modify-overwrite dance you would otherwise write by hand.

scenes.heading: Delta guarantees that make MERGE safe
scenes.narration: MERGE is only trustworthy because of Delta's underlying guarantees. The transaction log records each commit atomically, so a MERGE is all-or-nothing. Readers get snapshot isolation, seeing a consistent version even while the MERGE writes. And because every version is logged, you can time-travel back to inspect or restore the table before the change.

scenes.heading: MERGE vs overwrite
scenes.narration: A MERGE surgically updates only the rows and files it needs to, incrementally and atomically, which is efficient on large tables. A full overwrite rewrites the entire dataset every run, which is simple but wasteful and loses fine-grained change history. For incremental pipelines and CDC, MERGE is both faster and safer. Reserve overwrite for full refreshes where rewriting everything is genuinely intended.

scenes.text: Prune the target and keep files compact so MERGE stays fast.
scenes.narration: MERGE performance depends on how much of the target it must scan, so partition and Z-order on the match keys. Compacting small files keeps the rewrite step efficient.
